Construction will proceed in two phases, with an additional foundation of development and construction works worth ₹40 crore laid down where canals are replaced.

The inauguration coincides with a Diwali Milan function organized by legislator Ramakant Bhargava.

Both leaders had been apart after a rift widened following the government's removal of temporary constructions built by tribal people on forestland in Budhni. Senior BJP leaders later narrowed the divide, and Yadav met Chouhan in Delhi with several officers before attending the public function together.
items.title: MP Chief Minister and Union Minister to Inaugurate ₹536 Crore Irrigation Project

items.summary:
Severe storms brought flooding, strong winds, and widespread power outages across parts of the United States on Thanksgiving, disrupting holiday travel. Streets were inundated in New Jersey's Sea Isle City and Ocean City, with Avalon reporting some of its worst flooding ever; a few drivers had to be rescued after driving into floodwaters but no injuries occurred.

Macy's postponed its 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade in Manhattan until Saturday, citing caution about how the giant balloons would fare in windy conditions. The National Weather Service warned of disruption at eastern US airports through Friday morning due to poor visibility, turbulence, strong winds, and ice forming on aircraft.

More than 600,000 homes and businesses lost power Thursday afternoon, mostly in East Coast states, according to the outage tracking website poweroutage.us. Wind gusts of 80 km/h or higher were expected along Interstate 95, with all of New Jersey under a state of emergency declared by Governor Mikie Sherrill and parts of New York under one from Governor Kathy Hochul.

Rain and snow also hit Missouri, where up to 33 cm of snow was expected; heavy snow partly collapsed the roof of the Wentzville Ice Arena. On the West Coast, coastal flood warnings were issued from Southern California to Oregon and Washington because of king tides caused by aligned moon and sun gravity, and a wave tore down part of a pier in Pacifica, California.

Although both coasts faced flooding, travel is typically busier in the days leading up to Thanksgiving than on the holiday itself.
items.title: Thanksgiving Storms Flood US Coasts and Disrupt Travel

items.summary:
A paper by former senior Treasury officials John Kingman and Shriti Vadera argues that strong competition is essential to economic growth, but active pro-competition policy has become a blind spot in current UK government thinking.

The authors contend that about 60% of the fall in the UK's productivity rate since 2007 stems from reduced dynamism. They cite government Industrial Strategy Advisory Council figures showing firms under five years old accounted for 18% of all business sales in 2005, dropping to just 10% by 2021.

Kingman and Vadera claim ministers of both parties have grown less interested in competition as a growth source and more inclined to seek approval from incumbent businesses. They note that pro-growth interventions such as the City's big bang under Thatcher and the breakup of the BAA airport monopoly under Brown show past governments did support competition.

The paper says it has only been recently that active competition policy is viewed as a threat to growth rather than its driver, an attitude the authors say matters especially in the age of AI.
items.title: Former Treasury officials warn UK growth policy ignores competition

items.summary:
Former INX Media CEO Indrani Mukerjea told a court she did not meet her daughter Sheena Bora on April 24, 2012, the day prosecutors allege she was murdered. The accused also rejected claims that she used Skype to coordinate the killing.

Prosecutors allege Indrani, with former husband Sanjeev Khanna and driver Shyamvar Rai, killed Sheena on that date, then burnt her body and dumped it in Maharashtra's Raigad district. Investigators say the three attempted to kill Sheena's brother Mikhail as well but he escaped.

During court proceedings, Indrani was confronted with statements from approver Rai, who said she had instructed him to create a Skype account for his secretary Kajal Sharma so she could relay instructions about killing Sheena and Mikhail. Indrani denied ever speaking to Rai over the platform.

Rai also testified that Indrani asked him to arrange a car after he returned to India and accompanied him in searching for a location to dispose of the bodies, before allegedly contacting Peter Mukerjea. Indrani called this account false and denied making the call.

She further rejected allegations that she bought medicines prosecutors say were sedatives meant to be mixed with water and given to Sheena. The prosecution maintains these drugs would have been used against her daughter.

Former husband Sanjeev Khanna told the court he never met Sheena and had only seen Mikhail when he appeared as a witness during the trial. Peter Mukerjea said he knew nothing about the incident and was abroad at the time.

The accused denied all allegations as the trial continues.
items.title: Indrani Mukerjea Denies Meeting Daughter on Alleged Murder Date

items.summary:
Five months before France's presidential election, candidates turned the annual mayoral congress into a campaign venue to win endorsements from local officials. To qualify for the race, contenders must secure at least 500 endorsements from elected officials, with mayors representing the largest pool of potential sponsors.

Around forty figures have declared or are seen as possible presidential candidates, though not all will formally run. The Association of Mayors of France brings together roughly 34,000 municipal mayors, most elected without a partisan label.

David Lisnard, mayor of Cannes and head of the mayors' association since 2021, is pursuing his ambitions with his conservative Nouvelle Énergie party. He called for a stronger role for local government while criticizing excessive bureaucracy and contradictory regulations.

Lisnard's poll standing has risen amid divisions in the centre-right bloc, placing him ahead of former Prime Minister Édouard Philippe in some scenarios. Polls currently put far-right Marine Le Pen first, followed by left-wing Jean-Luc Mélenchon.
items.title: French Presidential Candidates Court Mayors Ahead of Election

visual.alt: Bar chart. Marine Le Pen (far-right National Rally) 500 endorsement; Jean-Luc Mélenchon (left, France Unbowed) 500 endorsement.

items.summary:
The collapse of Poundland has put 11,000 staff at risk of losing their jobs. A store manager in Camden said a colleague who had worked there for 11 years broke down when told about the situation.

This is described as the largest retail bust for a decade, with an estimated 600 high streets expected to lose an anchor store.

In 2025 Gordon Brothers bought Poundland for £1 and inherited a shareholder loan of £22.5m. The company reportedly rejected offers to buy the business over concerns about recovering that loan.

Poundland's founder, Steve Smith, warned that around 2,000 suppliers could be affected because most supply only to Poundland.

Liam Byrne, chair of the business select committee, estimated Gordon Brothers had already made £18.3m in fees and charges and would recover its £22m loan while restricting access to a £63m bank account used for restocking.

Byrne said he would change Section 172 of the Companies Act, which gives primacy to shareholders, arguing that such laws let private equity firms overload businesses with debt at the expense of jobs. He also called for employees to be placed on company boards in a German-style reform.

Union membership fell from 13m in 1979 to 6.5m by 2024, and pay as a proportion of GDP dropped from 72% in 1975 to 59% last year.

The article notes that union membership is associated with a 5.3% pay premium, based on figures from last year.
items.title: Poundland administration and the case for company-law reform

items.summary:
Retailers are increasingly relying on AI to optimize pricing during Black Friday, but this growing dependence may leave them more exposed to cyberattacks. According to Reuters, the technology is reshaping how discounts and deals are structured for the shopping event.

Brands have adopted AI tools to help price products so merchants can reduce discount depth without reducing demand. A co-founder of a price optimization platform noted that unlike human store managers who tend to slash prices to attract shoppers, AI 'has the confidence to hold its nerve.'

However, ransomware attacks on retailers occur 50% more frequently in November than at other times of year, and a broader surge in cyberattacks is raising concerns within an industry known for low levels of cyber insurance. A cyber executive cautioned that Black Friday should be treated as a resilience exercise just as much as a revenue opportunity.
items.title: AI Reshapes Black Friday Shopping While Raising Cybersecurity Concerns

items.summary:
The head of the World Health Organization urged the United States to lift its oil blockade on Cuba, warning that the restrictions are putting lives at risk.

Havana has long relied on discounted Venezuelan oil to cover an energy shortfall. Washington's removal of Nicolás Maduro and the resulting blockade have worsened Cuba's economic situation, prompting warnings of a humanitarian crisis.

Cuba's government blames the blockade for daily power outages and shortages of medical supplies. The island was already vulnerable before these measures were imposed.

The WHO chief said life expectancy in Cuba fell from 78.8 years in 2020 to 74.4 years in 2025, marking the first decline since records began in 1950.
items.title: WHO chief urges US to lift Cuba oil blockade

items.summary:
A Ukrainian drone strike that sank the Russian corvette Merkury in Benghazi risks reigniting Libya's civil war as rival factions scramble for leverage amid competing foreign interests.

The attack hit a Russian supply ship docked to refuel under an agreement between Moscow and eastern strongman Khalifa Haftar, whose Libyan National Army has vowed retaliation while its parliament ratified a Turkey-Libya maritime deal opening eastern waters to Turkish exploration that the EU calls null and void.

Ukraine's strike threatens a documented business partnership between the heirs of Libya's two rival families. According to the UN Panel of Experts' final report, Ibrahim Dbeibah's adviser and Saddam Haftar built control over the National Oil Corporation at every level of decision-making, creating Arkenu Oil Company, which diverted more than $3 billion through illicit fuel exports from January 2024 to November 2025.

The UN also documented an arms procurement pact between Dbeibah's government and Haftar's forces. By the panel's count, Libya's oil revenue in 2025 came to $18.78 billion excluding royalties and taxes against roughly $27 billion it should have earned. Saddam Haftar's office and a Tripoli official deny any connection to Arkenu.

The rival legislatures agreed on a unified budget, and Washington is drafting a merger that would keep Abdulhamid Dbeibah as prime minister while seating Saddam Haftar at the head of the Presidential Council. Armed western factions resist the plan, and Washington warned it could take measures against anyone who blocks it.

An influential Misrata military body demanded an end to the Arkenu deal earlier this month, declaring Libyan oil a red line. Two days after the strike, Dbeibah's government asked a Tripoli court to annul the contract. Jalel Harchaoui of the Royal United Services Institute says pressure on Dbeibah comes partly from powerful Misrata groups where Ukraine's drone teams are reportedly based.

The Merkury was hit in Benghazi's civilian port next to a naval base, and Kyiv says it escorted Russian convoys supplying Syria and Libya. Moscow sent investigators to Benghazi, and its ambassador said the strike will not go unanswered. Haftar's government opened a joint investigation with Russia and blamed treacherous Ukrainian aggression while Dbeibah's Tripoli government condemned the attack.

Russia could retaliate against western Libya but would need Haftar's bases since it lost Syrian ports after Assad fell and Turkey has kept the Turkish Straits closed to warships since February 2022. A strike on Misrata launched from those eastern bases would be read as a Haftar action, most likely to restart the war.

The Haftars face a balancing act: returning to war costs them their share of documented schemes and the Presidential Council seat Washington is offering Saddam, while refusing Moscow risks the patron that arms them. Their forces control fields and terminals feeding the NOC, Russia runs through their bases, and offshore acreage Turkey wants lies off their coast.

Dbeibah's government and Misrata stand to lose the US-backed premiership and eastern revenue arrangements, but hosting Ukrainian drone teams makes Misrata the likely target of any reprisal. Ankara has little leverage over Haftar despite recent meetings with his camp; Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalan met the Haftars in August 2025.

Turkey signed its maritime deal in 2019 with Fayez al-Sarraj, giving it a claim to drill off eastern Libya where TPAO already holds 40% of an offshore block northwest of Benghazi. Greece, Cyprus, Egypt and the EU say the deal is illegal under UN Law of the Sea.

A Russian strike on Misrata from Haftar's bases would put Turkish soldiers in the line of fire, undermine Turkey's drilling claim, and cost Haftar the backing he needs for Saddam's Presidential Council seat — likely triggering civil war.
items.title: Ukraine's Strike on a Russian Warship Risks Reviving Libya's Civil War

visual.alt: Bar chart. Reported revenue (excluding royalties and taxes) 18,780,000,000 $; Expected revenue -27,000,000,000 $.

items.summary:
US President Donald Trump said Thursday he had asked Vladimir Putin to 'pull back all military aggression' against Europe, marking a shift from the tone toward Russia's leader that characterized his meeting just one week earlier. The US president described Putin as his friend during their previous encounter.

Trump stated he made this request when he met Putin in China last week and said he believed it could help lead to an agreement ending Moscow's war in Ukraine against Kyiv, which he called a grinding conflict.

The comments came the day after Trump hosted NATO chief Mark Rutte in Florida. The two leaders issued a joint statement calling on Russia not to expand the Ukraine war.
items.title: Trump Urges Putin to End Military Aggression in Europe

items.summary:
The FBI unsealed an indictment charging Roberto Gómez, formerly known as 'Ruster,' with conspiring to help former Olympic snowboarder and Canadian cocaine kingpin Ryan Wedding operate what prosecutors call a billion-dollar drug trafficking empire. The case was filed in February 2026 in the Central District of California after remaining under seal.

Gómez is accused of participating in a conspiracy to assist Wedding, described as Canada's biggest cocaine trafficker, and of obtaining law-enforcement-sensitive information from Mexican authorities to help him evade capture, according to an FBI post on X. The indictment carries six counts against the sole defendant.

Prosecutors allege Gómez and Wedding used boats and aircraft to move hundreds of kilograms of cocaine from Colombia to Mexico, then shipped it into the United States by cargo truck through stash houses in Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino before moving shipments onward to Canada, their main market. Southern California served only as a stopover for this operation.

While Wedding hid in Mexico, Gómez reportedly sought to broker a deal selling him around 500 kilograms of methamphetamine valued at approximately $550,000, per court documents. By late 2025 the FBI had raised its reward for information leading to Wedding's capture from $10 million to $15 million.

Gómez reportedly preferred stablecoins such as USDT or Tether for making and receiving payments, shielding his profits from financial market fluctuations while acting as a broker of cocaine, methamphetamine and fentanyl across several Mexican criminal organizations.
items.title: Fugitive gang member Roberto Gómez indicted for helping Ryan Wedding run a billion-dollar drug operation

items.summary:
Morocco and Senegal both advanced to the round of 32 at the FIFA U-17 World Cup, though each team reached the next round despite a disappointing final group match.

Morocco finished second in Group H behind Spain with three points after losing 2-1 on Thursday. Defender Adama Soudi said his side struggled to find its rhythm against a strong Spanish team and could not recover once they fell behind, then had to move on from the defeat.

Senegal progressed after drawing 1-1 with Tajikistan in Group F, even though midfielder Konte was sent off. Coach Lamine Sane said his players became overconfident following their 9-0 win earlier and let themselves relax, which led to losing their number 10 in a dangerous challenge.

Ivory Coast, Morocco, Mali, Senegal and Mozambique have reached the next round, while Tanzania, Cameroon and Algeria are still fighting to qualify.
items.title: Morocco and Senegal advance to U-17 World Cup knockout stage

items.summary:
According to a new report by the Institute for Security Studies, Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) militants are expanding their technological capabilities to sustain their insurgency in Nigeria. The group has reportedly transformed commercial technology into weapons used for surveillance, propaganda, and combat.

The researchers say ISWAP has moved beyond drone surveillance, equipping commercial drones with improvised explosives and using them in attacks on military positions in northeast Nigeria. Armed drones, satellite communications, and international financing networks are central to this shift toward greater technological capacity.

The report also exposes supply and financing networks that stretch from Lagos and Kano to Dubai, alongside links to the Islamic State's central leadership. It further reveals a payment system that rewards fighters for weapons captured during military raids.

In response, researchers are urging Nigerian authorities to strengthen military bases, expand counter-drone capabilities, and disrupt the networks funding the insurgency.
items.title: ISWAP in Nigeria Turns to Armed Drones and International Financing Networks

items.summary:
A large-scale meta-analysis published in Psychological Bulletin found that earning more money tends to make people emotionally steadier and more responsible, while simultaneously making them lonelier and less empathetic.

The study combined 11 studies involving data from more than 130,000 people around the world. It was conducted by researchers at the Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Lead author Wendong Li said higher earnings were associated with greater emotional stability, a stronger sense of responsibility and improved problem-solving abilities. He also found that richer individuals became less agreeable and less extroverted, spending more time alone.

Li was surprised by how much wealth could reduce people's consideration for others. He suggested this may stem from the difficulty of understanding another person's circumstances once one's own daily reality drifts far away from theirs.

The researchers also noted that earning more money tends to encourage more conservative behavior, with higher earners becoming less willing to take risks or explore new possibilities.
items.title: Study finds higher income is linked to greater emotional stability but also reduced empathy

items.summary:
The AI-driven surge in data center energy demand is pushing the U.S. toward an all-of-the-above approach to power, with enhanced geothermal emerging as a promising zero-emissions alternative that borrows drilling technology from the oil industry.

Enhanced geothermal aims to make geothermal energy viable anywhere by drilling deep enough—three, four, or even six kilometers—to reach uniformly hot rock and then fracturing it horizontally while piping in water. The heated rock turns the water into steam that spins turbines to generate electricity.

University of California Irvine engineer Mohammad Javad Abdolhosseini Qomi said this approach could unlock more than enough geothermal energy underground to power the entire United States, though he noted safely and economically unlocking it remains a major challenge.

The U.S. Department of Energy's Genesis Mission backs UC research into enhanced geothermal and projects that such projects could provide about 90 gigawatts of carbon-free energy in the U.S. by 2030, enough to power at least 65 million homes.

Big Tech is backing the sector through deals like Quaise Energy signing a major power purchase agreement with Google to supply 50 megawatts (MW) of superhot geothermal power beginning as soon as 2030. The article attributes this forecast and deal details to Oilprice.com reporter Haley Zaremba.
items.title: Enhanced Geothermal Energy Borrows Drilling Technology From Big Oil

items.summary:
On November 20, Vietnam's National Assembly approved a revised penal code that removes capital punishment from six offenses, including drug trafficking and rape of minors. When the law takes effect in March, only four crimes — treason, murder, terrorism and illegal drug production — will remain death-eligible, down from 44 offenses in 1997.

The reforms come as Vietnam's Communist Party intensifies its crackdown on political dissent, prompting officials to describe them as humanitarian and proportionate. General Luong Tam Quang said the changes reflect a tougher approach to crime overall while reducing capital punishment for some categories.

Experts characterize the shift as selective rather than complete abolition. Hai Luong of Griffith University called it 'retentionist-but-reductionist,' noting Vietnam modernizes its legal system without giving up severe penalties for serious crimes. Tran Dai Lam, an ANVI lawyer, said effectiveness now rests on certainty of prosecution more than punishment severity.

The changes follow a year earlier when the National Assembly removed capital punishment from eight other offenses including embezzlement and espionage. Existing death sentences for abolished offenses can be commuted to life imprisonment. The EU welcomed the reduction as positive but stressed that drug-related executions without intentional killing still fall short of international standards.

Execution numbers remain uncertain because Vietnam classifies them as state secrets. Amnesty International believes capital punishment is still used extensively, though it cannot provide reliable annual figures. Daniel Pascoe of City University of Hong Kong warned reforms may simply shift charges toward remaining death-eligible offenses like drug production.

Vietnam joins a broader Southeast Asian trend away from executions. Cambodia, the Philippines and East Timor have abolished the penalty entirely; Malaysia removed mandatory sentences in 2023; Indonesia's new code allows commutation after a probationary period. In contrast, Singapore has increased use of capital punishment while Myanmar resumed executions in 2022.

According to Amnesty International, 17 countries carried out executions in 2025, including China, Saudi Arabia, Yemen and the US. Sara Kowal of Eleos Justice noted that number is near an all-time low but flagged Iran and Singapore as exceptions where use appears rising.
items.title: Vietnam Narrows Death Penalty as Regional Trend Continues

items.summary:
Moscow said Thursday it hopes a November meeting between President Vladimir Putin and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi will help improve bilateral relations, Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova stated at a news conference in Istanbul. The remarks marked Russia's first official confirmation of the roughly 30-minute informal talks held on Nov. 18 during the APEC summit in Shenzhen, which were the first face-to-face encounter between the two leaders since September 2019.

Citing Japanese sources, Kyodo News reported that Takaichi called for the immediate release of detained journalist Yuki Imai and urged Russia to retract measures placing Japan Tobacco Inc.'s Russian assets under domestic control. The meeting came after Moscow-Tokyo ties deteriorated sharply following Japan's sanctions on Russia amid the Ukraine war.

Zakharova described recent Baltic border closures as 'openly hostile actions,' saying Russia reserves the right to retaliate politically and diplomatically. Her comments followed Estonia's decision, announced by Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna, to close all crossings from Dec. 1 after its Internal Security Service attributed an attempted arson attack on drone manufacturer Threod Systems to Russian military intelligence.

Lithuania's border guard chief Donatas Skarnulis said closing its borders was unnecessary at present, while Latvia's Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs said Riga was considering the step but needed careful consideration. Moscow rejected accusations that Russia ordered the Estonian attack.

Zakharova also accused Kyiv of trying to provoke a direct confrontation between Russia and NATO countries to escalate the war and derail negotiations. She further alleged that European officials' willingness to negotiate with Moscow concealed 'an ongoing aggressive sentiment toward Russia in Europe.'

The spokeswoman commented on the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity, a proposed transit corridor linking Azerbaijan's Nakhchivan exclave through southern Armenia, noting it drew criticism from Iran. The project stems from an August 2025 Washington summit where Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev and Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan initialed a peace agreement with US President Donald Trump mediating.
items.title: Russia Hopes Putin-Takaichi Meeting Improves Ties; Moscow Warns Over Baltic Border Closures

items.summary:
A study of smallholder sheep farmers in Limpopo, South Africa, found that the vast majority rely on uncontrolled mating rather than planned selection to grow their flocks. This practice may limit productivity gains even among well-adapted local breeds.

Researchers surveyed 70 households in Makurung and Lenting villages near Lebowakgomo, interviewing only families keeping at least five sheep. The majority had between six and ten years of farming experience and mostly kept Dorper or mixed Dorper-Meatmaster stock developed for hot, dry conditions with limited grazing.

About half of the farmers said they keep sheep mainly for savings, investment and meat production rather than milk or wool. Most strikingly, 90% practised uncontrolled mating instead of choosing which males breed with which females.

Farmers did express clear preferences: for rams they valued mating ability, body size and growth rate; for ewes the top traits were producing twin lambs, mothering ability and short lambing intervals. But these choices may overlook reproductive anatomy that signals breeding potential.
items.title: Most smallholder sheep farmers in South Africa use uncontrolled breeding

visual.alt: Bar chart. Savings, investment and meat production as main purpose 48.8 %; Practised uncontrolled mating 90 %.

items.summary:
Meta has launched its Muse AI assistant in countries including the UK, US, Canada, Australia and Japan. The tool can shop for users, book tickets and conduct negotiations on their behalf.

Muse requires customer permission before making purchases, connecting to apps or using bank details autonomously. However, companies worry that employees might link their personal assistants to work emails and databases.

The UK Information Commissioner's Office says firms using agentic AI must show ongoing compliance with data protection law. This includes identifying steps to mitigate risks of harm to users and the wider public.

This item asks employers and senior managers whether they have concerns about Muse and similar tools, including any examples where such technology has failed or caused problems.

It also seeks details on what measures companies are taking to manage these issues, such as updating guidance or issuing new advice to employees about handling agentic AI.
items.title: Meta Rolls Out Agentic AI Assistant Across Key Markets Amid Employer Concerns

items.summary:
A University of the Western Cape PhD researcher found that South Africa's entrepreneurship education is too theoretical, with no integrated mentorship or hands-on practice to prepare students for entrepreneurial careers.

The research examined how curriculum design and teaching methods could better equip young people for business ventures. The study was conducted by a doctoral student in collaboration with professors Chux Gervase Iwu and Zivanayi Nyandoro.

Focus group discussions were held with 60 students in their third and fourth academic years at two South African universities, where three-quarters had taken entrepreneurship as part of an economics and business studies programme while a quarter had never encountered the subject.

Participants reported that teaching methods did not provide practical experience such as project-based tasks or developing business plans. They also said mentorship was absent from their curricula and gave them no access to formal mentoring relationships with experienced industry practitioners.

Students who were not mentored described feeling less confident about their skills and being less likely to attempt running a venture after graduating.
items.title: South African study finds business graduates lack mentorship and practical experience

visual.alt: Bar chart. Youth (aged 15-35) 56.78 %; National 33.9 %.

items.summary:
The World Nuclear Association argues that radiological protection rules should shift from a strict linear no-threshold model toward a simpler, risk-informed and proportionate system at very low doses. The group says current over-conservatism wastes public funds, regulatory effort and industry resources on negligible risks while fueling fear.

Its position statement claims there is clear epidemiological evidence of health risk only above about 100 millisieverts (mSv), with limited or no consistent evidence below that level. It notes the linear no-threshold approach assumes risk rises in proportion to dose down to zero, but accepts it as a practical basis while urging it be applied alongside a graded approach rather than alone.

The association says residual risks at very low doses are extremely small compared with everyday life and sit within natural background radiation, which averages about 3 mSv per year worldwide. It points out that eating one banana gives 0.0001 mSv while two return transatlantic flights give the same dose as a full year working in nuclear power stations.

The group says over-conservative clearance criteria can force material to be managed as radioactive waste at high cost, and pushes five recommendations for regulators: adopt proportionality; pursue optimisation rather than minimisation; acknowledge uncertainty at very low doses; update international guidance; and set a practical cut-off below which no further effort is needed.

The statement was developed by the World Nuclear Association's Radiological Protection Working Group in consultation with radiation protection practitioners, supported by its technical report 'Decision-Making at Very Low Doses.' The association represents more than 280 companies across the nuclear value chain.
items.title: Nuclear industry calls for graded approach to very low radiation doses

visual.alt: Bar chart. Eating one banana 0.0001 msv; Dental X-ray 0.005 msv; Return London to New York flight 0.08 msv; CT scan of the chest 6.6 msv; Average yearly radon dose in UK 1.3 msv; Typical airline crew member 3 msv; Nuclear power station worker 0.18 msv.

items.summary:
The European Union has approved EUR 1.2 million in grant funding to help Montenegro build a distribution grid flexibility platform, according to the country's power utility Elektroprivreda Crne Gore (EPCG).

A steering committee of the EU Integration Facility backed EPCG's proposal for a system that would monitor various energy resources and align their operation with what the distribution grid needs.

The project's first phase is valued at EUR 1.5 million, according to EPCG, with the remaining amount coming from national sources rather than the EU grant.

EPCG developed the platform together with Montenegro's distribution system operator CEDIS, the University of Montenegro's Faculty of Electrical Engineering, and the Ministry of Energy and Mining.

The pilot will connect battery storage systems, electric vehicle charging stations, prosumers, and other distributed energy resources to a central monitoring and control system under real grid conditions.

The platform is designed to collect and process energy data, produce forecasts, and apply artificial intelligence to optimize how connected resources operate.

EPCG says the pilot results will form the basis for wider deployment of these solutions across Montenegro's distribution grid.
items.title: EU approves funding for Montenegro's distribution grid flexibility platform

items.summary:
The Netherlands has opened tenders for the IJmuiden Ver Gamma-A and Gamma-B offshore wind sites, which together represent up to 2 GW of new generating capacity in the North Sea.

Each site can accommodate about 1 GW. The Gamma-A area covers roughly 129 square kilometers and sits approximately 53 kilometers off the Dutch west coast, while Gamma-B spans around 95 square kilometers at a distance of about 61 kilometers offshore.

The two wind farms will share one 2 GW offshore platform operated by transmission system operator TenneT. That platform connects to the electricity grid through a direct-current link that brings power ashore at Maasvlakte.

The Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO) is handling permitting, with permits for both projects expected in the first quarter of 2027 and scheduled operation targeted for 2032. Construction schedules and final investment decisions are to follow once developers win the tenders.
items.title: Netherlands Opens Tenders for IJmuiden Ver Gamma-A and Gamma-B Offshore Wind Sites

items.summary:
A century after its serialization, Upton Sinclair's 1926–7 novel Oil! is being revisited for its prescient critique of capitalism and the oil industry. First published in The Daily Worker, the book later inspired Paul Thomas Anderson's film There Will Be Blood.

Set against California's 1910s oil boom and America's entry into World War I, the novel traces how crude oil fuels modern civilization while exposing the inequalities behind it. Sinclair likened its role to whaling in Moby-Dick, treating oil as the supreme metaphor of modernity.

Sinclair conceived Oil! after witnessing a 35-metre geyser strike by Shell Oil near his Long Beach property in 1921. He recalled watching investors scramble over 'liquid gold,' describing it as seeing human nature completely naked. The novel dramatizes the full supply chain of oil from extraction to consumer.

The book extends radical journalism like Mary Tarbell's 1904 exposé on Standard Oil, but Sinclair believed fiction could make complex economic forces more comprehensible than reporting. He told a family member in 1925 that this 'oil novel will be the best thing I have ever done'.

At 550 pages, Oil! follows young James 'Bunny' Ross Jr., who learns about class conflict and oil's corrupting influence as his father builds an empire. The narrative spans themes from automobile industry growth to Prohibition, religious revivalism, Hollywood propaganda, spiritualism, and birth control.

The novel foreshadowed Sinclair's own 1934 gubernatorial campaign, when MGM head Irving Thalberg attacked him in newsreels that historian Greg Mitchell called the 'birth of media politics.' Oil! also anticipated his later Pulitzer Prize-winning Lanny Budd series.

The piece concludes with global energy figures: roughly 100 million barrels of oil are burned daily and about 42 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide enter the atmosphere annually. The author invokes Fredric Jameson's idea that it is easier to imagine the end of the world than capitalism, framing Sinclair as a guide to that challenge.
items.title: Upton Sinclair's 'Oil!' Revisited as a Century-Old Anti-Capitalist Epic

items.summary:
At a high-level dialogue in Geneva marking 25 years since China joined the World Trade Organization, Li Chenggang, China's international trade representative and vice minister of commerce, said multilateralism is essential for addressing global challenges. He called on all parties to use WTO reform as an opportunity to strengthen the multilateral trading system and enhance its role in global economic governance.

Li reflected that China used accession to deepen domestic reform, noting that respecting international rules underpins integration into globalization while reforms tailored to national conditions turn opening-up opportunities into development gains. He stressed continued commitment to common development, citing unilateral full-coverage zero-tariff treatment granted to all African countries with which China has diplomatic relations and to least developed country partners.

WTO Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala praised China's economic growth, poverty alleviation, technological innovation, and contributions since accession. She said the experience provides an example for other developing members seeking integration into the multilateral trading system and commended China's capacity-building assistance through South-South cooperation. Okonjo-Iweala expressed hope that China would continue to play a constructive role in WTO reform.

More than 200 participants attended the event, including ambassadors and deputy permanent representatives from major WTO members as well as representatives of international organizations, media outlets, and think tanks. Discussions covered China's achievements over the past quarter-century and ways to uphold the multilateral trading system and promote inclusive economic globalization.
items.title: China Reaffirms Commitment to WTO-Centered Multilateral Trading System

items.summary:
The inaugural China-Mongolia-Russia international passenger train (V3/4) from Beijing to Irkutsk arrived at Ulan Bator Railway Station on Thursday afternoon, marking the start of a new weekly cross-border service.

The route spans all three countries and covers about 2,666 kilometers over roughly 55 hours. Border inspection and immigration take place at designated crossings in China (Erenhot), Mongolia (Zamiin-Uud and Sukhbaatar), and Russia (Naushki).

Cao Li, chargé d'affaires ad interim of the Chinese Embassy in Mongolia, said the service aims to boost cross-border trade, people-to-people ties, and the China-Mongolia-Russia Economic Corridor.

The round-trip runs weekly. Train V3 departs Beijing Railway Station every Wednesday at 7:27 a.m., while the return train V4 leaves Irkutsk Railway Station every Saturday at 6:58 a.m.
items.title: China-Mongolia-Russia passenger train arrives in Ulan Bator

items.summary:
IBM has discontinued H-1B visa and green card sponsorship for the majority of foreign workers in its US consulting business, reportedly giving affected employees three weeks to relocate abroad or resign by year's end. Those who leave will receive three months' severance pay with December 31 as their final working day, according to The Indian Express.

The company cited changing client requirements and shifting availability of skilled workers rather than attributing the decision directly to US immigration policy. In a statement quoted by The Indian Express, IBM said its participation in high-skilled visa programs had been declining for years as skill availability and client needs evolved.

The move comes amid broader tightening of US immigration under President Donald Trump's second term, which began in 2025. In October, the US suspended IT companies including Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL, Capgemini, Microsoft and Adobe from the Permanent Labor Certification Programme that allows employers to sponsor foreign workers for employment-based green cards.

Indians have made up a large share of recent visa recipients, comprising 71% of all H-1B visas issued in financial year 2023-'24. The Indian Express reported that IBM's decision is likely to impact several Indians.
items.title: IBM Ends Visa and Green Card Sponsorship for Most Consulting Workers

items.summary:
India's Parliament is set to hold a special session beginning November 30, with the delimitation bill as its central agenda item. This follows April's defeat of the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill by a united Opposition that denied the government a two-thirds majority. NDA managers now believe they may reach or approach the required threshold after an unprecedented churn in which lawmakers from several parties joined hands with the BJP.

Delhi's air quality was rated 'poor' at 8am Thursday, when the Central Pollution Control Board recorded an AQI of 220 and a 24-hour average of 224. Thirteen of 57 monitoring stations read 'very poor,' while 27 were in the 'poor' category and 17 moderate; Delhi Technological University logged the highest reading at 335, with Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium lowest at 130.

US President Donald Trump defended Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang amid national security scrutiny over China ties. Speaking from Mar-a-Lago, Trump said he did not consider Huang a threat and had enough information to support his view; AFP reported that Trump described Huang as happy about returning for what he calls his 'second term.'

The 2026 Fide World Chess Championship between Javokhir Sindarov and Gukesh D produced its third consecutive draw on Thursday. The game lasted almost five hours over 60 moves, with Sindarov unusually holding position in his chair during the first hour.

Author Amish Tripathi defended Nitesh Tiwari's film 'Ramayana' for depicting Sita as a warrior who fights asuras and practices swordplay. In an interview with Screen, Tripathi noted that various versions of the Ramayana exist, including three attributed to Valmiki, one in which Valmiki also portrayed Sita slaying Ravana herself.
items.title: HT Morning News Brief for November 27

items.summary:
Nvidia has instructed its manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers with advanced AI chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia as the United States tightens export controls aimed at preventing Chinese companies from accessing restricted computing technology through overseas data centres.

The suspension follows a US Commerce Department interim final rule titled 'Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors,' which took effect on November 19. The rules add licensing requirements for exports of advanced chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, countries Washington views as higher-risk diversion channels.

Manufacturing partners including Dell and Super Micro Computer reportedly told customers in the four Southeast Asian countries that Nvidia would not authorise their orders. The duration remains unclear because the move appears intended as a temporary measure while Nvidia and its partners assess compliance requirements under the new framework.

China is excluded from the suspension list because Washington already restricts direct exports of advanced processors to China through separate rules. The latest measures target a different problem: Chinese firms renting computing capacity remotely from data centres in third countries rather than buying chips directly, an arrangement that Southeast Asian operators have used to serve customers like Alibaba, Tencent and ByteDance.

The suspension arrives amid scrutiny over Singapore-based Megaspeed International, an Nvidia partner under investigation for allegedly diverting advanced chips or servers containing them to China. The controversy also drew attention to Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive linked to someone connected with China's Ministry of State Security. US intelligence officials examined whether Chinese intelligence sought information from her.

Huang resigned before the board reinstated him as CEO on November 23 following intervention by President Donald Trump. Prosecutors have not established that she was directed to collect information about Huang or that she passed substantial intelligence value to China, and Beijing has rejected espionage allegations.

Nvidia executive Jay Puri's relationship with Cenly Chen, former chief growth officer at Super Micro Computer, also drew scrutiny after the couple married on March 7, 2026. The attention intensified following a Justice Department charge against Super Micro co-founder Yih-Shyan 'Wally' Liaw for conspiring to smuggle more than $500 million worth of servers containing Nvidia chips into China.

Prosecutors alleged that at least $510 million in equipment was diverted through a Southeast Asian company. Neither Puri nor Chen appeared in the indictment, and Super Micro maintained it was a victim while denying involvement in chip procurement.
items.title: Nvidia Halts AI Chip Shipments to Four Southeast Asian Countries Over China Diversion Risk

items.summary:
Shares of several Tata group companies rose on Friday after a Bloomberg report said the Tata Trusts filed a lawsuit challenging Natarajan Chandrasekaran's reappointment as chairman of Tata Sons Pvt Ltd. The filing, according to people familiar with the matter quoted by Bloomberg, signals an escalating power struggle at the top of the $185-billion Indian conglomerate.

The stocks in focus included Tata Power Company Ltd, Tata Steel Ltd, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd, Tata Consultancy Services Ltd (TCS), and Tata Chemicals Ltd. These companies are among others within the broader Tata group that drew attention following the reported legal action.
items.title: Tata Trusts Sues Tata Sons Over Natarajan Chandrasekaran Reappointment as Chairman

items.summary:
A report by Axis Bank Economic Research says the Reserve Bank of India may consider a sharper 50-basis-point repo rate hike at its upcoming December MPC meeting, though it keeps a 25 bps increase as the base case.

The bank cites resilient economic growth and persistent inflation as reasons for more aggressive tightening. It projects second-quarter GDP growth at 7.6% with gross value added rising 8.3%, driven by government spending, strong consumption, and easier working capital credit.

Inflation is expected to stay above the RBI's upper tolerance threshold of 6% until at least June 2027, according to the report. The bank also points to growing second-round effects as rising input costs increasingly pass through to goods and services prices.

Accelerating credit growth has been flagged as another sign of economic overheating in the analysis. If demand stays strong and inflation does not ease toward 5% in FY28, rates may need further increases that could push the terminal policy rate to about 6.5%, roughly 50 bps above the estimated neutral rate.

Interest rate swaps currently price in a 50 bps increase for December, reflecting expectations of tighter monetary conditions. The report suggests a larger hike would give the RBI room to pause later and reassess economic trends.
items.title: Axis Bank Report Points to Possible 50 Bps RBI Rate Hike in December

visual.alt: Bar chart. Q2 GDP growth % 7.6 %; GVA growth % 8.3 %; Inflation upper threshold % 6 %; Target inflation FY28 % 5 %; Terminal policy rate % 6.5 %; Projected bond yield % 7.5 %.

items.summary:
The Ministry of Manpower reported on November 27 that Singapore's full-time employed residents saw their real median income rise by 2.2% in 2026, down from 4.1% the previous year.

Real income growth for workers at the 20th percentile slowed to 1.3%, compared with 3.6% a year earlier, indicating smaller gains for lower-wage earners.

The ministry said the slower pace partly reflected more cautious wage increases by firms and higher inflation, which it projected would rise around 2% in 2026 versus 0.9% in 2025.

The figures are preliminary because full-year 2026 inflation data is not yet available.

Despite weaker gains for lower-wage workers in 2026, the ministry noted their incomes have grown faster than median incomes over recent five- and 10-year periods, with continued support from progressive wage measures.
items.title: Singapore real incomes grew slower in 2026, with lower-wage workers gaining least

visual.alt: Bar chart. Median full-time employed residents (2026) 2.2 %; Median full-time employed residents (2025) 4.1 %; 20th percentile workers (2026) 1.3 %; 20th percentile workers (2025) 3.6 %.

items.summary:
Singapore's job-switching rate fell to 5.7% of employed residents in the year ending November 2026, continuing a gradual downtrend from its 2022 peak as hiring slowed and workers sought stability, according to the Ministry of Manpower (MOM).

Among full-time resident employees aged 25 to 64 who changed jobs, about two-thirds, or 65.6%, saw their incomes rise after inflation, with most gains reaching at least 5%.

Over a longer five-year span from 2021 to 2026, roughly 67% of job switchers enjoyed higher real incomes compared with about 61% who stayed put, MOM's Ang Boon Heng said at the November 27 media briefing on the advance labour force report.

More than nine in ten switches over the past year were voluntary rather than caused by retrenchments. Among involuntary switchers, only around 58% saw wage gains versus about 67% of those who left voluntarily, so job stayers and involuntary movers were less likely to out-earn their previous roles.

Younger residents below 30, especially the 15-to-24 age group, cut switching most sharply and cited stability for staying. Older workers aged 50 and above switched least, with about half holding jobs of at least a decade.
items.title: Fewer Singapore Workers Changed Jobs in 2026, but Most Who Switched Earned More

visual.alt: Bar chart. Voluntary switchers (2025-2026) 67 %; Job stayers (2025-2026) 61 %.

items.summary:
Apple's iPhone Air received a significant price cut during Reliance Digital's Black Friday sale 2026, bringing the slim device closer to the ₹90,000 price segment. The article is titled around an effective discount of ₹32,000 on this deal.

The 256GB variant was listed at nearly ₹1.2 lakh before the promotion and is now available with a direct discount of almost ₹25,000. This brings the base price down toward the lower end of Apple's premium iPhone range.

An additional bank offer stacks onto the direct discount to further reduce the effective purchase price, making this one of the more attractive iPhone deals during the ongoing sale.
items.title: iPhone Air gets ₹32,000 effective discount in Reliance Digital Black Friday sale 2026

items.summary:
A spokesperson for China's Ministry of Commerce firmly opposed the United States' proposed additional Section 301 tariffs on China and other economies, calling them a unilateral act that violates World Trade Organization rules.

The Office of the US Trade Representative announced results from its Section 301 investigation into alleged overcapacity, proposing to impose additional Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies including China. The Ministry of Commerce spokesperson said this investigation is a typical example of unilateralism that disrupts the international economic order.

Spokesperson He Yadong argued the US was using 'overcapacity' as a pretext for protectionism, politicizing normal market competition and turning industrial development into political tools. He warned these practices would push up global inflation, harm businesses and consumers, and create long-term risks to global economic growth.
items.title: China Opposes New US Section 301 Tariffs on Overcapacity

items.summary:
A road accident left Pakistani patient Yasir Ali with multiple fractures that previously would have required a roughly 600-kilometer journey to Karachi, according to the report. The GDA Pak-China Friendship Hospital now allows patients in Makran, Balochistan, to receive surgery closer to home.

Yasir underwent treatment at the hospital and spent about seven days there before beginning recovery. Nearly two months later, he had returned to work.

The case is presented as an example of how China-Pakistan healthcare cooperation makes quality medical services more accessible to local communities.
items.title: Pak-China Friendship Hospital Provides Local Treatment for Balochistan Patient

items.summary:
The Narendra Modi government appears ready to accept sweeping tariff and non-tariff concessions in exchange for a marginal improvement in its access to the American market, risking India's trade leverage as Washington pursues unilateral Section 301 tariffs. On November 25, US Trade Representative Ambassador Jamieson Greer announced an intention to impose a 25 per cent tariff on Indian goods over alleged subsidies and excess capacity, while offering a reduction to 17 per cent if New Delhi agreed to what the article describes as a fair and reciprocal deal.

The proposed agreement would grant highly subsidised American agricultural exporters, pharmaceutical companies, and industrial producers zero-tariff or preferential access to India's market of about 1.4 billion people, including roughly 300 million classified as affordable middle class. The author argues that the one-percentage-point advantage Indian exporters might gain over competitors barely offsets the losses from opening this enormous domestic market.

India's response has been described as weak: New Delhi denied having structural excess capacity in any sector and insisted trade concerns be handled within ongoing negotiations, even though Brazil called for a WTO dispute panel against similar Section 301 tariffs. The article contrasts India's posture with that of the Modi government versus Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's administration, which reportedly said it would not bend to American tariff threats.

The piece also notes China accused Washington of political manipulation over its own higher combined tariffs and pointedly recalled a 2020 WTO panel ruling against US Section 301 tariffs that the United States then voided by blocking Appellate Body appointments. The author frames these measures as part of a pattern in which each expired or struck-down legal instrument is replaced, with IEEPA tariffs overturned by the Supreme Court and earlier Trade Act tariffs expiring.

The article concludes that India should weigh not just tariff reductions but the reciprocal concessions, surrendered market access, and lost policy space required for what it calls a MEGA deal at the G20 summit next month. The author warns that in its eagerness to strike an agreement with Washington, India may abandon multilateralism, reciprocity, and sovereign trade policymaking.
items.title: India May Concede Trade Leverage to Secure Tariff Reduction With Trump

items.summary:
A DC Edit opinion piece contends that the Trump administration's plan to raise tariffs on Indian goods signals gradual erosion of American economic supremacy rather than protecting it.

The proposed tariff increase would lift duties on Indian imports from 10 per cent to 25 per cent under Section 301, according to recommendations from the US Trade Representative (USTR).

These proposals emerged from a USTR investigation into the economic policies of 16 economies accused of creating structural excess manufacturing capacity that harms American commercial interests.

The article states these 16 economies and the United States together account for roughly three quarters of global economic output and more than two-thirds of international merchandise trade, though this figure is presented as a claim without sourcing.

USTR identified five alleged unfair practices in India: manufacturing subsidies, weak worker rights protection, capital allocation distortions, market access restrictions, and insufficient efforts to curb overcapacity linked to non-market economies like China. India rejected all allegations, asserting it has no structural excess capacity in any sector.

The editorial defends the government's right to impose tariffs as an exercise of economic sovereignty when domestic industries face threats or job losses.

However, the author disputes the core premise that higher import costs will restore US manufacturing and jobs, arguing countries like China and India have built sophisticated ecosystems beyond simple labor cost advantages.

The piece adds that any manufacturing returning to the United States may be increasingly automated, producing fewer jobs than expected.

As its central argument, the article emphasizes what it calls America's greatest structural advantage—the dollar's status as the world's principal reserve currency—which enables favorable borrowing and large deficits. The author claims steep tariffs on allies despite this privilege indicate that American economic dominance is fading.
items.title: An editorial argues Trump's India tariffs reveal a weakening US economy

items.summary:
The Centre has broadened its crackdown on Zakir Naik's Islamic Research Foundation (IRF) by empowering state governments and Union Territory administrations to freeze funds and restrict access to properties linked to the organisation. The move follows a five-year ban extended by the home ministry days earlier.

A notification issued Thursday delegated these powers to states and UTs under Section 42 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, directing that all authorities exercisable by the Centre under Sections 7 and 8 of the UAPA shall also be exercised at the state level in relation to the banned association. The Central Government issued this direction.

The powers trace back to the home ministry's November 13 declaration of the IRF as an unlawful association, made under sub-sections (1) and (3) of Section 3 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, through notification S.O. 6182(E).

Section 7 empowers authorities to prohibit use of funds belonging to a declared unlawful association by issuing written orders barring anyone holding money, securities or credits from paying, transferring or otherwise dealing with them without government permission.

A gazetted officer authorised under Section 7 can inspect premises, examine records and investigate financial transactions suspected of being linked to the organisation. Section 8 lets authorities notify any place believed to be used for an unlawful association.

After such a notification, the district magistrate may prepare an inventory of movable property at the premises and restrict entry by people who were not residents when the order was issued. Police officers of at least sub-inspector rank can search individuals entering or found there.
items.title: Centre expands powers over states and UTs in crackdown on Zakir Naik's IRF

items.summary:
Swapan 'Babun' Banerjee, younger brother of former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and uncle of TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee, approached police on Thursday seeking registration of an FIR against his nephew over alleged threats and obstruction to a blood donation camp, according to news agency PTI. The complaint was filed at the Kalighat police station.

Babun said he had witnessed intimidation during the TMC's 15-year rule in West Bengal and that such incidents continued after the BJP came to power in May this year, claiming to have observed them since 2024. He cited obstruction of government work, forcible takeover of clubs, and intimidation as examples.

Details of the blood donation camp incident and the specific allegations against Abhishek Banerjee were not immediately available at the time of reporting. The complaint comes amid a long-standing estrangement between Babun and Mamata, who had previously declared that she severed ties with him.

The family discord has taken on political dimensions following the BJP's victory in West Bengal assembly elections, which ended the TMC's uninterrupted 15-year rule. Since the change of government, Babun has grown closer to BJP leadership and repeatedly praised chief minister Suvendu Adhikari.

Babun recently invited Suvendu Adhikari to inaugurate a community Durga Puja in his neighbourhood and was seen touching the chief minister's feet during the event. His repeated public admiration for Suvendu has fuelled speculation about his political leanings and possible shift toward the BJP, though Babun has not made any formal announcement of joining the party.
items.title: Mamata Banerjee's Brother Seeks FIR Against Nephew Abhishek Over Alleged Threats

items.summary:
Historic king tides and a climate-amplified super El Niño drove record-high coastal flooding across Southern California during the Thanksgiving holiday week. In Los Angeles, the tide peaked at 8.19 feet above average low tide, tying last month's record, while La Jolla waves also broke records just after setting them.

Climatologist Daniel Swain attributed the elevated water levels to an overlap between king tides and the super El Niño rather than storms. Assistant professor Joseph Lucey-Renteria said conditions were expected to worsen in December before returning to similar levels, but noted residents had been spared large waves.

Residents responded with makeshift defenses as streets closed and businesses posted 'Closed' signs behind sand bags. Lara Mitry's Sunset Beach home escaped damage while her neighbor Jerry Cimmarusti set up close to 300 sand bags; in Naples, Long Beach, neighbors raised sea walls about two feet using plywood.

Long Beach had put a $125 million sea wall retrofit project on hold earlier this year after costs ballooned and an oil production decline created budget pressure. The project has resumed but is progressing slowly, leaving 90-year-old eroded walls further deteriorating with each tidal swing.
items.title: Southern California Coastal Communities Brace for Historic Thanksgiving Flooding

items.summary:
A weekend of severe weather is forecast across Australia, including bushfires on Flinders Island, heavy rain and flooding in Tasmania and Victoria, storms across eastern states, and intense heatwaves in northern regions.

On Flinders Island, firefighters are battling an out-of-control bushfire that has destroyed or damaged at least eight buildings. The northern deputy regional chief of the Tasmania fire service, Steve Richardson, warned conditions would be hot and dry with winds up to 30km/h gusting to 50-60km/h.

Residents in several areas were told to take shelter after it became too late to leave, while others were advised not to return. An evacuation centre is open at the Furneaux Arts and Entertainment Centre.

The Bureau of Meteorology's Sarah Scully said heavy rain would hit northern Tasmania with six-hourly totals of 40-70mm and a risk of flash flooding early Saturday morning. Flood watches are in place for several coastal rivers, including Forth, Mersey, Meander, North Esk, Tamar, Ringarooma and the north coast.

In Victoria, rain began falling on Friday afternoon under a severe weather warning covering damaging winds from south-west to north-east. Six-hourly totals of 55-70mm were likely, with isolated falls up to 110mm possible and gusts up to 100km/h expected in the north-east Saturday morning.

Some parts of Victoria's Mallee and Wimmera had already received a month's worth of rain in about an hour. Yaapeet, a town of about 75 people in western Victoria, got 63mm in six hours including roughly 36mm in one hour, far exceeding the region's expected monthly total.

Victorians voting on Saturday could expect conditions to ease from mid-to-late morning, though showers and storms remained possible. Storms with heavy rain, damaging winds and large hail were forecast across eastern states from southern Queensland through northern and central NSW, including Canberra and Sydney.

By Sunday, the rain band and thunderstorms would shift into north-east New South Wales and south-east Queensland, including parts of Brisbane. Prolonged heatwaves in northern Australia were expected to intensify to severe or extreme levels in western Australia's Kimberley, with temperatures reaching the mid-40s, while Perth could see high 30s.

The article notes that global heating from fossil fuel burning has increased the frequency and severity of such extreme weather events.
items.title: Australia Braces for a Weekend of Extreme Weather, From Bushfires to Floods

items.summary:
Philippine ex-president Rodrigo Duterte goes on trial at the International Criminal Court (ICC) on Nov 30 for the 'crime against humanity of murder' over killings that occurred between 2011 and 2019. Photographers who documented those deaths are reflecting on their work as his case proceeds.

Noel Celis, a freelance photographer who worked for AFP at the time, photographed about 200 drug war killings during the crackdown. He said he still reacts with fear when a motorcyclist pulls up beside him at a red light, describing the two-man teams that roamed Manila dealing out death as 'riding in tandem.'

Celis's most defining image showed a young woman cradling the bloody body of her boyfriend after he was gunned down at a busy intersection. To the mainly Catholic nation it resembled Michelangelo's La Pieta and quickly became the emblematic picture of the crackdown.

The journalists initially called themselves 'nightcrawlers,' named after a Hollywood film about Los Angeles camera crews chasing late-night mayhem. At first police had no problem alerting them to killings, but they stopped sharing information as public outcry grew, forcing photographers to chase mortuary vans summoned by police to collect the dead.

Dondi Tawatao, 46, recalled returning with AFP to a garbage-strewn street on a rainy night about 10 years ago where he photographed two bodies beneath the exposed roots of a banyan tree. He believed two handguns near them were planted there and described the scene as 'very dark' and sinister.

Tawatao said after shooting the drug war for four years, killings became so normalized that he stopped visiting crime scenes unless they involved at least three corpses. The long nights reshaped how he saw Manila, giving him a mental map of where people had been killed.

Kimberly dela Cruz, 36, found her first victim on Manila's rail tracks and another atop a major bridge. At the second scene she said the head of the man was wrapped in packaging tape next to a poster reading 'I'm a drug pusher, don't emulate me.'

Dela Cruz said some colleagues required professional counseling, with one suffering recurring nightmares about the dead coming back to life. She noted that residents of the mainly slum-area killing grounds could fear journalists as much as police.

Celis's memories centered on the keening of victims' wives and mothers and the sharp smell of blood. He said photographers wrestled with guilt over not being able to help and accusations of profiting from others' suffering.

When Celis and a colleague attended the wake of the La Pieta victim, they half-dreaded a lynching by angry relatives. They went partly to apologize for their inability to help and told the girlfriend that the pictures could serve as evidence if charges were ever brought.

Tawatao said all photographers interviewed believed the drug war did not solve the country's narcotics problem and remained convinced police murdered thousands to enforce Duterte's will. Celis added that Duterte 'ordered a war on drugs that killed many people' and called his death toll 'the natural consequence of his actions.'

Celis argued that photographs are powerful, especially now when he said standing history on its head is in vogue. Tawatao alluded to Holocaust deniers, saying the photos provided incontrovertible proof that the killings happened.

None of the photographers thought Duterte's arrest and handover to the ICC last year was possible until it occurred. Tawatao said he was shocked because they had only seen those in power get away with such acts. Dela Cruz described a huge sense of relief when Duterte was flown to The Hague, saying it meant some justice for families.
items.title: Photographers Reflect on Duterte Drug War as He Faces ICC Trial

items.summary:
The Allahabad High Court remarked that the legislature may consider reducing the age of juvenility from 18 years to 16 years, following a similar observation by the Kerala High Court.

Justice Abdul Shahid made the remark while dismissing a juvenile's appeal against rejection of his second bail application in a dacoity-murder case. The order was dated November 17.

The Kerala High Court had earlier observed that it is high time for legislatures to amend statutes dealing with juveniles and children in conflict with law, noting the present trend showing sufficient maturity among children at age 16.

Justice Shahid said this aspect may be duly considered by the legislature after taking note of the Kerala court's observations about maturity attained by children upon reaching 16 years.
items.title: Allahabad High Court says legislature may lower juvenile age to 16

items.summary:
Binance announced Thursday that it has completed its withdrawal recovery work and lifted the suspension on withdrawals following a record $6.3 billion theft in a hack last month.

The platform clarified that only a small number of networks remain temporarily paused for maintenance or planned upgrades, which is separate from the finished recovery effort.

Binance published this statement on November 27, 2026.
items.title: Binance lifts withdrawal suspension after record $6.3 billion crypto heist

items.summary:
A BJP legislator from Hubballi-Dharwad West criticized the government for celebrating Japan's Kawasaki Heavy Industries investment while North Karnataka receives little manufacturing support. The politician, identified as Bellad on X, said the Rs 800 crore agreement is being hailed as a boost to Karnataka's manufacturing sector but pointed out that it goes to Harohalli near Bengaluru rather than North Karnataka.

The legislator questioned whether industrial development in the state 'begins and ends with Bengaluru and its surrounding districts' and argued that greater investment in North Karnataka was necessary to address longstanding regional disparities. He said 'North Karnataka deserves its fair share of investments, industries and opportunities.'

Earlier, Shivakumar welcomed Kawasaki's plan to invest about Rs 800 crore over the next 10 years to expand Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery at Harohalli, calling it an endorsement of Karnataka's industrial capabilities.

The expansion is planned in two phases and will manufacture hydraulic pumps, swing motors and other components used by the construction-equipment industry. It is expected to create around 600 jobs.

Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery was established in Bengaluru in 2012 and has produced more than 2 lakh hydraulic pumps and motors. The MoU was signed in Tokyo in the presence of Industries Minister MB Patil.

Shivakumar said Karnataka has more than 525 Japanese establishments and attracted 101 Japanese greenfield projects since 2016, adding that the government would support the proposed expansion and further strengthen the state's manufacturing ecosystem.
items.title: BJP MLA Questions Kawasaki Investment Location in Bengaluru

items.summary:
The British Embassy in Tokyo is urging young British men to be cautious about a rise in drink-spiking incidents targeting foreign visitors across Japan. The embassy released its first post in a series this week, noting that recent spiking cases have focused on British men aged 20 to 30.

Drink-spiking refers to adding alcohol or drugs to someone's food or drink without their consent. According to data from the U.K.'s Foreign and Commonwealth Development Office (FCDO), spiking cases in Japan have risen by more than half over the past seven years, with male victims accounting for about 93% of those incidents.
items.title: British Embassy Warns Young Male Visitors of Drink-Spiking Risk in Tokyo

items.summary:
Yadav said the SP has prepared a separate document detailing how it would finance its five-year poll schemes within the state's annual budget of around Rs 1 lakh crore.

He stated that officials with financial and administrative experience were involved in assessing the feasibility of major decisions, though he gave no further detail on the funding mechanism itself.

Citing the Agra-Lucknow Expressway as an example, Yadav said his government initially considered building the 302-km project under a public-private partnership model but banks did not extend support. He added that it was subsequently built through the EPC model using the government's own budget at a cost of around Rs 15,000 crore.

On restoring the Old Pension Scheme for government employees, Yadav acknowledged technical complications involving funds held under the National Pension System and said the party would set up a committee to work out the details. He reiterated an assurance first given in 2022 that the scheme will be implemented.
items.title: SP leader Yadav outlines funding plan for Uttar Pradesh poll promises

visual.alt: Bar chart. Agra-Lucknow Expressway (EPC model) 150,000,000,000; Planned expressway length 302.

items.summary:
Tokyo Electric Power Company Holdings said Thursday it would review its plan to complete an anti-terrorism facility for the No. 7 reactor at its Kashiwazaki-Kariwa nuclear power plant in Niigata Prefecture by August 2029.

The contracting company has informed Tepco that construction needs to be extended by more than a year because of factors including labor shortages, according to the power supplier. No revised completion target has been set.

This delay is expected to further push back the restart of the reactor after Tepco previously moved the facility's completion from October 2025.

An anti-terrorism facility also remains incomplete for the plant's No. 6 reactor, which was restarted in January this year and cannot continue operating unless that facility is finished by April 2031.
items.title: Tepco delays Niigata nuclear plant anti-terrorism facility completion

items.summary:
A jury has convicted former Queensland Royal Australian Air Force pilot Robert Crawford of the murder of his wife, Frances Crawford.

Frances Crawford died at her Upper Lockyer property in July 2024 after being discovered fatally injured near a toppled ride-on lawnmower. She was found trapped beneath the machine before she died.

Crawford pleaded not guilty and maintained that he had pulled his wife from under the approximately 200-kilogram lawnmower and tried to revive her, believing she may have died while moving it away from automated sprinklers during his sleep. Prosecutors alleged instead that he strangled her, manipulated her body and the scene, then called emergency services with a false account.

The jury heard testimony from more than 40 witnesses, including three defence experts, before deliberating for over three days to reach its verdict.
items.title: Former RAAF pilot Robert Crawford found guilty of murdering his wife

items.summary:
Premiership-winning halfback Sam Walker has signed a two-year deal with the Papua New Guinea Chiefs to play in their inaugural season of the 2028 NRL campaign.

The 24-year-old Queenslander, who broke his relationship with the Sydney Roosters after the club's grand final victory, will head to Port Moresby following what he described as the best year of his career, which included State of Origin and Australian Test debuts.

PNG Chiefs coach Willie Peters praised Walker's vision, kicking ability, creativity, game control, and experience performing at club, state, and international levels. He said Walker's partnership with Jarome Luai gives the team one of rugby league's most creative halves combinations.

General Manager of Football Michael Chammas said the Chiefs identified Walker as a player who could have a transformational impact on how they play and build their side. He described Walker as a premiership winner, Origin star, and World Cup winner whose best years are still ahead.

Walker is part of a wave of signings for the PNG Chiefs, who have attracted attention by offering tax-free contracts. In the past week alone, they signed Canberra and New South Wales backrower Hudson Young and North Queensland star Jeremiah Nanai.

Luai, Brian To'o, Zac Lomax, and Joseph Manu will also feature in the Chiefs' inaugural season. Walker is the ninth player the team has signed who holds either Test or Origin experience.
items.title: Sam Walker Signs Two-Year Deal With PNG Chiefs for 2028 NRL Season

items.summary:
US President Donald Trump said Thursday that he asked Vladimir Putin during their meeting in China last week for Russia to 'pull back all military aggression' against Europe, expressing hope it would help reach a quick agreement ending the war. The remarks came after Trump hosted NATO chief Mark Rutte and issued a joint statement calling on Russia not to expand the conflict.

Trump told reporters he did not know whether Putin would attend the G20 summit scheduled for December 14-15 in Florida, but said the Russian leader 'certainly can' come if he wanted. He acknowledged some people might object to Putin's presence and doubted Putin himself wished to attend, though Trump added that personally he would like to have him there.

Trump described Putin as wanting 'to make a deal' to end the war, saying his priority was stopping the loss of life on both sides. During a Thanksgiving call with US military personnel from Mar-a-Lago in Florida alongside First Lady Melania Trump, he reiterated his desire for an agreement with Moscow.

When pressed about calling Putin his friend while also criticizing Russian aggression, Trump said maintaining cordial ties is important to securing peace and that 'we want to make a deal. We want to stop killing.' He cited reports of Russia losing 25,000 people a month in the war and compared strained diplomacy to the hostility between Zelensky and Putin.

Trump dismissed investigations into alleged Russian interference in US politics as a 'fake' investigation before reaffirming that his discussions with Putin had been positive. He said they 'had a very good discussion,' noting he has known Putin for a long time, and concluded that 'the bottom line is he would like to make a deal.'

Trump's remarks underscored his focus on negotiating an end to the Ukraine war while signaling continued diplomatic engagement with Moscow. However, it remains unclear whether Putin will respond to Trump's appeal or take concrete steps toward reaching a peace agreement.
items.title: Trump urges Putin to end Ukraine war aggression and signals openness to peace deal

items.summary:
Sheikh Hasina has set 16 December as the date for her planned return to Bangladesh and said she is willing to walk across the border if no flight from Delhi can be arranged, putting Dhaka on edge while complicating relations with New Delhi.

Hasina fled to Delhi in August 2024 after a student-led uprising ended her 15-year rule. She was sentenced to death for crimes against humanity in an absentia trial and faces arrest and execution if she returns; the UN says as many as 1,400 people were killed by security forces during the unrest.
